chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn Uthman said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, as for fish, what is permissible to eat from them?' He said, 'That which has scales.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say about the sea bass (kandath)?' He said, 'There is no problem with eating it.' I said to him, 'But it does not have scales.' He said to me, 'Yes, but it is a fish of bad disposition; it buries itself in everything, and if you look at the root of its ear, you will find scales on it.'

key_terms.الْكَنْعَتِ: Sea bass (a specific type of fish)

ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for determining if a fish is halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the nuanced juristic methodology of the Imams, who often provided specific biological details to clarify general principles for the layperson. It demonstrates the principle of 'takhassus' (specification), where a general rule regarding scales is refined by identifying the anatomical location of scales in the sea bass (kandath), thereby resolving apparent contradictions in culinary permissibility.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, fro Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! The fishes, what can we eat from these?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever had scales for it’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the Sea bass. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘But it does not have scales for it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes, but it is a fish of evil creation. It goes beneath everything, and when you look in the roots of its ears, you will find scales on it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, of fish which kind is edible?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The kind of fish that has scales is edible.’ I then asked, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what do you say about al-Kan‘at (a kind of fish with very little scales). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful to use it for food.’ I then said, ‘It does not have scales?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it has scales but it is a bad mannered fish and it sticks to everything. If you look at the base of its ears you can find scales.’”
